passes.title: Retail autopilot drone with tag and phone
passes.note: Every part a first complete build would want, priced from retail. This is the starting point for every reduction.

passes.title: Used autopilot, Pi Zero streams video, ground station runs detection
passes.note: A used autopilot saves most of the big flight-controller cost. The Pi Zero streams video, and a phone or laptop on the ground runs detection. Risk added: control now depends on the ground link, so the autopilot's own link-loss failsafe must be tested in simulation. The close-range ToF is dropped until logs show a need.

passes.title: Printed frame and guards
passes.note: Printed structure replaces the commercial frame. Risk added: printed parts fail differently from machined or moulded ones, so every printed load-bearing part needs a bench stress test before flight.

passes.title: Bench-first kit (no flying drone yet)
passes.note: Buy only what the bench rig needs: a Pi Zero, a camera, the tag, and filament. Sensors and companions are tested on a desk and the replay tool gets real logs. The flying parts wait until those logs justify them. The Tello is optional for indoor follow-logic tests.

passes.title: Owned phone replaces the Pi and camera on the drone
passes.note: A spare phone already has a camera, GNSS, an IMU, Wi-Fi and enough compute for small detection models. Risk added: the phone adds weight, needs its own battery and mounting, and its power and heat behaviour is untested. Only try it after bench tests.
